newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES STABLE AHEAD OF TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES STABLE AHEAD OF TENDER.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market held steady to their overnight levels on Thursday with dealers saying market players were sitting on the sidelines waiting for results of the weekly treasury bill tender.

"Rates are unchanged from yesterday because people are waiting for the tender results. Maybe the tender bill will go up slightly, because there's demand for paper. We don't know yet," one dealer said.

The buying rate for NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days remained at its overnight 22 percent, as did the selling rate at 21.5 percent while bankers' acceptance bills were also quoted unchanged at 21.5 percent (buying) and 21 percent (selling).

The call rate remained fluctuating in a 15 to 20 percent range with the central Reserve Bank indicating a market surplus of Z$300 million at the start of Thursday's session due to maturing treasury bills.
This was an improvement on a shortage of Z$55 million indicated on Wednesday.
